budget_tradeoff_detail: Ablates number of contexts N and per-context length l (Fig. 4); best reported config N=32, l=768 tokens/context, success rate 77.32% (Table 2).
confound_note: Context-type ablation (Fig. 3) compares Prompt-Proposals/rule-based, BM25 lexical, and RandomNN embedding retrieval as the source of repo context while context length/number are held fixed, isolating the retrieval-mechanism effect from budget.
stop_detail: Fusion-in-Decoder architecture independently encodes each of N retrieved repo contexts (each appended to 2-line surrounding hole context via special tokens) then jointly attends over concatenated encodings during decoding (Sec. 3).
threats_to_datum: Best-performing variant (Prompt-Proposals) is a heuristic rule-based extractor rather than a learned retriever, so gains attributed to 'retrieval mechanism' may partly reflect heuristic quality rather than the FiD architecture itself.

key_numbers.metric: Execution accuracy (ChatGPT backbone), EVOR vs DocPrompting

budget_tradeoff_detail: Sec. 4.4 reports pass rate as a function of token consumption swept 4k-24k, showing diminishing returns; EVOR's iterative loop consumes ~4x the tokens of DocPrompting for its accuracy gain (Table 7).
confound_note: Primary comparison (EVOR vs Reflexion/DocPrompting, Table 2) varies both knowledge source diversity (docs+web+exec-feedback+code vs single static source) and the iterative query-evolution mechanism jointly, at unmatched token budgets; the repo-level SWE-bench-Lite result is a secondary, less-instrumented experiment.
stop_detail: Iterative loop (Algorithm 1) evolves the retrieval query each round using prior generated code and execution errors, retrieves via INSTRUCTOR-xl dense embeddings (or BM25) over a knowledge base that itself grows with execution feedback, capped near 4,096 tokens (Sec. 3).
threats_to_datum: The paper's primary knowledge base is external documentation/web/execution-feedback rather than repository files; the only genuine cross-file repository-context instantiation is a secondary SWE-bench-Lite experiment treating 'repository content as documentation' with no structural (non-flat) treatment, weakening its relevance as a structure-aware repo-context datum.

venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology (TOSEM) — accepted, revised/extended version
budget_tradeoff_detail: Retrieval corpus chunked at max 2,000 tokens/chunk (Java) and 1,000 tokens/chunk (Rust) (Sec. 3.1.3); type-context graph pruned to direct neighbors and stdlib types removed to bound prompt size (Sec. 3.2.1).
confound_note: Headline comparison against RepoCoder varies both the representation (added type-dependency graph) and the retrieval mechanism (hybrid BM25+dense with RRF vs RepoCoder's iterative retrieval) simultaneously; component-level ablation (Table 7, removing -CR or -TC individually) is the only isolated comparison.
stop_detail: A static analyzer (Eclipse JDT / rust-analyzer) builds a directed type-dependency graph of field/signature context pruned to direct neighbors, concatenated with hybrid BM25+dense-retrieved (RRF-fused) code snippets into the generation prompt (Sec. 3.1.3, 3.2.1, Fig. 4).
threats_to_datum: Because RepoCoder differs in both representation and retrieval mechanism from CatCoder, the reported +17.35% pass@5 gain cannot be attributed cleanly to the type-dependency-graph representation alone without relying on the separate component ablation.

demote_reason: Full text confirms every problem is a single, isolated Verilog module with a provided testbench (VerilogEval-Human v2); the Task-and-Circuit-Relation-Graph and AST-based waveform-tracing tool are single-module internal representations built per-problem, with no multi-file/multi-module repository structure, cross-file dependencies, or repository-scale context budget ever addressed.

key_numbers.metric: Pass@1 (Claude-3.5-Sonnet, full K-Trans vs prompt-engineering baseline)

confound_note: Ablation removes knowledge types (dependency usage examples, code samples, translation pairs) progressively and varies knowledge-base maturity (0/50/100%, Table 6) without holding total prompt token budget constant across arms; multiple LLM backbones also compared.
stop_detail: For each focal function, retrieves target-language code samples and translation pairs via BM25 (Elasticsearch) then re-ranks with UniXcoder embedding similarity, plus tree-sitter-extracted dependency usage examples, assembling a chain-of-thought translation prompt with self-debugging (Sec 2.2-2.3).
threats_to_datum: Single benchmark (RustRepoTrans, 375 tasks, self-constructed) and no independent replication; knowledge base built partly from the paper's own translation history.

confound_note: Component ablations (multi-chain generation, multi-agent debate, edit plan) tested one-at-a-time on the same DeepSeek-V3-0324 backbone with fixed graph-traversal breadth/depth (K=5,W=4,L=5); prompt/token budget across arms not reported or controlled.
stop_detail: Builds a static code dependency graph (calls, inheritance, imports, variable references) via static analysis, traverses it with BFS+DFS from K seed entities to form K×W fault-propagation localization chains, then runs a 3-round multi-agent debate per chain before MCTS-based patch generation (Sec 3).
threats_to_datum: Evaluated only on SWE-bench family (Python repositories); graph-construction accuracy depends on the static analysis tool and is not independently validated.

key_numbers.metric: Agentless score cited from surveyed work

budget_tradeoff_detail: Notes budget as a general concern ("large repositories exceed context limits, making selection critical", Sec 4.1.2) but performs no cross-method token/cost comparison itself.
confound_note: N/A - literature synthesis, not a controlled comparison; taxonomizes graph-based vs non-graph retrieval substrates (Table 3, Sec 4.2) descriptively rather than benchmarking them against each other.
stop_detail: Organizes repository-level RACG into context construction, retrieval optimization, generation, and environment-interaction stages, taxonomizing graph-based (edge/node types, Table 3) vs embedding/AST-based retrieval substrates (Sec 4).
threats_to_datum: Coverage depends on search/selection strategy (v1 Oct 2025, revised through May 2026); no independent verification of numbers cited from surveyed papers; does not aggregate cross-method comparisons on shared benchmarks.

key_numbers.metric: Resolution rate, full system vs base (SEC-bench Lite)
Cost per issue, base vs full
Token share of context/report-generation stage (full config)

budget_tradeoff_detail: Full pipeline (CPCAgent+SPAAgent) raises per-issue cost from $0.0296 to $0.0718 while raising resolution rate from 48.8% to 75.0% on SEC-bench Lite; context/report-generation alone consumes 70.45% of tokens in the full configuration (Sec IV-A).
confound_note: CPCAgent and SPAAgent are added incrementally on top of a base workflow; both context representation and total token/cost budget vary together across the ablation arms, so gains are not isolated to representation choice alone.
stop_detail: CPCAgent incrementally collects code context via a code-search toolkit and clangd-backed symbol analysis (find-definition/find-references) until convergence, producing a Context Analysis Report that enriches the issue report before localization and patch generation (Sec III/IV-B1).
threats_to_datum: Evaluated only on C/C++ projects (SEC-bench, 13-29 projects); clangd-dependent tooling may not generalize to other languages; $ cost figures are tied to specific LLM API pricing at time of study.

demote_reason: The paper is an experience report on a three-tier agent-memory infrastructure (constitution, 19 domain-expert agent manifests, and a keyword-searched knowledge base of 34 spec documents) for a single 108K-line C# project. It indexes conventions, orchestration protocols, and design-intent documentation, not source-code structure, and states no token-budget mechanism for repository code context beyond keeping the constitution 'concise enough to fit every session' (Sec 3.1). There is no cross-file structural representation of code (no AST/call-graph/skeleton) and no budget-vs-quality tradeoff for code context, so it has no cross-file-structural-budget concern.

key_numbers.metric: extra token savings over SWE-Pruner baseline on multi-turn tasks (matched compression)
key_numbers.value: 7-14% more tokens saved; 30.5% total reduction vs 23.1% for SWE-Pruner with Sonnet 4.5

key_numbers.metric: head-to-head win rate on multi-turn comparisons
Exact Match / Edit Similarity gain on LCC at 8x compression

budget_tradeoff_detail: At matched 4x/8x compression targets, LaMR saves an additional 7-14% tokens over the SWE-Pruner baseline on multi-turn agent tasks while improving Exact Match by up to +3.5 on single-turn tasks (Sec 4.2, Table 3).
confound_note: Compression ratio (budget) is held constant between LaMR and the reproduced SWE-Pruner baseline (Sec 4.1: 'all methods are evaluated under matched compression constraints'); only the pruning representation/mechanism (single CRF vs. dual-rubric CRF + MoE gating) varies.
stop_detail: In-loop middleware intercepts file reads and prunes raw code-text lines via two dedicated CRFs (semantic evidence, dependency support) fused by a mixture-of-experts gate, then an AST-aware post-processing pass restores scope/control-flow headers and referenced imports (Sec 3.4).
threats_to_datum: The SWE-Pruner comparator is a reproduced baseline rather than the original paper's reported numbers, and headline token-saving percentages aggregate across benchmarks rather than being benchmark-specific.

token reduction range across four MLLMs with multimodal integration

key_numbers.value: accuracy drops 13.6-34.1 points; cost rises up to 268%

budget_tradeoff_detail: Text+graph multimodal integration cuts input tokens 4.8-46% and cost up to 26% across four MLLMs while maintaining or improving issue-resolution accuracy; a vision-only setup instead raises cost up to 268% and drops accuracy 13.6-34.1 points (Table 2; RQ1/RQ2).
confound_note: The central comparison (text-only vs. vision-only vs. multimodal SeeRepo) varies both representation and modality, and token/cost are the measured outcomes rather than held constant, so this is an ablated/measured comparison, not a budget-matched one.
stop_detail: During agent exploration, an external tool returns a Graphviz-rendered PNG of a distance-aware dependency subgraph (contains/imports/invokes/inherits edges) centered on the query target, with the agent autonomously controlling traversal depth, alongside standard text-based repo navigation.
threats_to_datum: Results are per-model averages over three runs on a 500-instance and a 110-instance benchmark using Graphviz-rendered images specifically; generalization to other renderers or MLLMs beyond the four evaluated is untested.

demote_reason: Full text (arxiv.org/html/2607.16372) confirms AoA operates entirely over the AST of a single proof/theorem within one interactive theorem-proving session; its token/cost/tool-call savings come from replacing serialized source-text proof states with a fused JSON AST + tree-edit representation for that one proof, not from managing cross-file structural budgets across a repository. The only repository-scale mentions (seL4 kernel ~70k proof goals, ~140k historical goals; Why3-derived NTP4VC-Pearl) are motivational framing for why per-proof token cost matters at scale, not something the method addresses -- no multi-file/codebase/project-level context selection or budgeting is performed. Out of scope for structure-aware repository-level context engineering.

key_numbers.metric: Failures attributable to missing/mislocalized vulnerable files or lines

budget_tradeoff_detail: No explicit token-budget-vs-quality tradeoff curve reported; agents are given context windows of at least 256K tokens (Sec 4.1) and explore repos via unindexed shell commands, but the paper does not quantify how detection/localization quality changes as a function of budget size.
confound_note: Central comparisons vary model (Qwen3.5 2B/4B/9B/27B, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GLM-5.2, MiniMax-M3) AND agent scaffold (Claude Code, OpenHands, MiniSWE) simultaneously across the same benchmark tasks -- capability, scaffold, and effective exploration budget all confound together; no single-factor ablation isolates representation or mechanism alone.
stop_detail: Agents receive no pre-built structural index; they explore repositories turn-by-turn with read-only shell commands (find/ls/grep/rg/cat/head/tail/sed) to locate vulnerability-relevant code, with performance decomposed into end-to-end detection plus three oracle-based subtasks (critical-operation localization, entry-point identification, trace construction) (Sec 4.1-4.3).
threats_to_datum: Key numbers are best per-cell results pulled from multi-row Tables 2-3 (many model x scaffold combinations), not a single headline system result; extracted via WebFetch text summarization of the HTML rather than direct inspection of rendered tables, so exact adjacent-row values are unverified.
